near_miss.rationale: Claim no retraction exists when both channels are empty; the empty map is one, although the coproduct itself is empty.
Count retractions onto the difference channel as |S|^|PD| instead of |PD|^|S| (9 for sizes 2, 3 instead of 8).
Claim a retraction onto the structure channel exists because the difference channel is nonempty; with an empty structure channel no map from a nonempty difference channel into it exists.
Claim a pair of maps into the empty set has a unique extension when both channels are nonempty; there are no such maps at all.
Read the DAG sentence "no reduction of either channel to the other" as nonexistence of a retraction for two inhabited channels; retractions exist whenever the target channel is inhabited.
Claim a structure item can coincide with a difference item inside the coproduct; the injections have disjoint ranges.
Claim the structure channel always reads as a difference even when the difference channel is empty; then no map from structure items to difference items exists.
Treat the reduction as unique; when it exists there are |A|^|B| choices and the coproduct selects none.
Count maps out of a coproduct by adding the counts for the two channels instead of multiplying.
Claim Real_0 has an element when neither channel is posited; the construction alone yields none.
Claim positing a structure channel posits a difference channel; the two posits are independent.
Claim that not every pair of maps out of the channels extends to the coproduct; the universal property gives exactly one extension for every pair.
Swap which channel a retraction lands in: with an empty difference channel the retraction onto structure exists, not onto difference.
Take the coproduct of two one-element channels to have one element (a join) instead of two.
